subject: Predict() with 1 Categorical Covariate and 2 Continuous Covariates

messages.author: 67eefb0e32c64fae
messages.subject: Predict() with 1 Categorical Covariate and 2 Continuous Covariates
parts:
Hello! This forum has been super useful recently - and I hope some of my solutions have helped others.

I am trying to predict detection probability as a function of 3 variables: Region (SiteCov with 2 levels), Effort (continuous ObsCov) & Experience (continuous ObsCov). But I keep getting an error when I try and use the predict function. My code for this is below...

#Model with 3 Covariates
fmRC <- colext(psiformula = ~1, gammaformula = ~1, epsilonformula = ~1, pformula = ~unlist(SR) + obs.effort + obs.exphrs, data = FosnUMF, se = TRUE)

#Setting up Dummy Variables for Predict
newDataRC <- data.frame(SR = factor(rep(c('EGB','SWC'))), obs.effort = 4, obs.exphrs = 200)

#Data Frame for Predict
> newDataRC
   SR obs.effort obs.exphrs
1 EGB          4        200
2 SWC          4        200

#Error I get with Predict
predict(fmRC, newdata = newDataRC, type = 'det', appendData=TRUE)
Error: ncol(coefficients) == length(obj@estimates) is not TRUE

messages.author: ab7bbe167f897cdd
messages.subject: Re: Predict() with 1 Categorical Covariate and 2 Continuous Covariates
parts: There is probably a mismatch in the number of levels of the Region variable. Check to make sure the number of levels in the model building dataset (FosnUMF) is the same as the predict dataset (newDataRC). Use str() to check both, and possibly droplevels() if needed.
